description.purpose: The workspaces of the space (R-27-7): `ws_open`, `ws_status`, `ws_diff`, `ws_patch`, `ws_merge`, `ws_commit`, `ws_discard`, `ws_tree`. A workspace is pointers only -- `ws_files` rows appear at the first touch (copy-on-write) and every new version is made by `./write` over `in_put` (`patch`, `merge3`, `create`). A commit is two-phase with one commit point, a single `commits` row going `prepared` -> `committed`; the heads after it are brought forward idempotently by whoever meets a lock next (`in_recover`, or the next `ws_commit` over the file).
description.use_when: Inside a file space only, behind `in_ws` and `./write`'s `in_recover`.
description.not_in_scope: No content of its own (no diff applied, no merge computed here), no workspace inside a workspace, no rebase or stash, no answer to `in_recover`.
description.emits_meaning: `ws_store` to `./store` between phases (`phase` names the job), `in_put` to `./write` (answer on `put`), `in_derive` once per file a commit moved, `answer` once per request.
description.consumes_meaning: A request on `in_ws`, a commit to finish or abort on `in_recover`, `./write`'s `put` answers, the store's answers to its own bundles.
